body.statement: Set \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\), and construct \(\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) using the rule \(\underline D_{H,n}\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\) separately for every finite-stratum response set \(H=F_\kappa\), every breakpoint response set, and the terminal response set \(H=F_\infty\). Uniformly over all data-generating laws satisfying the maintained model, \(\Pr\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). The reported upper endpoint is \(+\infty\) whenever the separately tested terminal stratum \((K,+\infty)\) is retained. If \(D_\infty(P)>0\), the probability of rejecting the terminal stratum and declaring a finite upper endpoint converges to one.
body.justification: One simultaneous multinomial event covers the entire identified set and propagates numerical error without a multiplicity penalty over switching-cost values.
body.gap: Tamer--Walker develop generic Bayesian inference for PMF-indexed identified sets, while this theorem is a finite-sample frequentist inversion specialized to the finite-versus-infinite terminal frontier.
body.consumer: Empirical users obtain a uniformly valid confidence set that does not spuriously replace an observationally admissible infinite ceiling by a finite number.
